newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to approve flax aid controls on Monday.
newsitem.headline: EU to approve flax aid controls on Monday.

text.p: European Union farm ministers are expected to approve on Monday new controls to ensure that flax subsidies are only paid to farmers who sell their crop, EU diplomats said.
The controls follow a 30 percent increase to 134,133 ha in the EU flax area in the 1996/97 crop year and a 70 percent rise since 1989/90.
EU aid payable to flax producers in 1996/97 totals just over 116 million Ecus, given an aid rate of 865.48 Ecus per hectare.
"There is a widespread feeling that the subsidy system has been abused," said a diplomat.
Another said that some farmers were growing flax only in order to obtain EU subsidies.

The biggest increase has been in Spain where the planted area has surged to 46,613 ha in 1996/97, from zero in 1992/93. Britain has also expanded flax plantings, though officials say that there are market outlets.
Spain, which objects to farmers having to achieve minimum flax yields per hectare in order to qualify for subsidies, is expected to vote against the new controls.
France wants the subsidy controls, notably a compulsory contracts between farmers and processors, to be extended to hemp producers.
France, Belgium and the Netherlands are traditional flax producers. --Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
